name: Myristyl stearate
description: Myristyl stearate (CAS 17661-50-6 ), also known as tetradecyl stearate, is a fatty acid ester derived from myristic alcohol and stearic acid. It functions as a lubricant, emollient, and rheology modifier across personal care and industrial formulations. Solid at room temperature, it contributes waxy texture, slip, and consistency to a broad range of end products. In personal care, it is used to build structure and improve skin feel in stick formulations and pressed powders. It is frequently utilized in cream-based cosmetics where a smooth, non-greasy payoff is required. Lip balms, solid perfumes, and deodorant sticks rely on its waxy binding properties to achieve the desired hardness and application texture. In lubricant and metalworking applications, it acts as a solid lubricant additive, reducing friction in formulations where controlled viscosity and film-forming behavior are priorities for the manufacturing process. It also functions as a dispersing aid in pigment-loaded systems, improving homogeneity in wax blends and color cosmetics. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for formulators seeking consistent performance. Myristyl stearate is supplied as a white to off-white solid, typically in flake or pastille form. Cosmetic-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with specifications aligned to personal care industry requirements. Technical-grade material is available for industrial and lubricant applications.
